parts.title: Kite Day
parts.text: It was a **windy** day at the park. Tomas, Lily, and Aziz brought a red kite. Lily’s coat began to **billow** like a sail. “Hold the string!” said Tomas. The kite began to **flap** in the air.

parts.title: Up It Goes
parts.text: Aziz ran fast, and the kite went up with a **whoosh**. It began to **zigzag** across the sky. Then it started to **whirl** in a circle. Tomas felt a **tug** on the string.

parts.title: A Tangle
parts.text: Oh no! The string began to **tangle**. It made a **loop** around Aziz’s foot. He began to **flail** his arms. Lily gave the string a **yank**, and it came free. Then the wind grew **breezy** and soft.

parts.title: Back on the Grass
parts.text: The kite floated down to the grass. The friends sat down and ate a snack. “Next time we will hold on tighter,” said Aziz.

definitions.meaning1: To puff out and fill with air, like a sail. Example: The sheet will billow on the clothesline.
definitions.meaning2: A big, rolling cloud. Example: A billow of steam came from the pot.
definitions.studentChallenge: The flag began to ___ when the wind filled it.

definitions.meaning1: To go left, right, left, right in sharp turns. Example: The ant will zigzag across the path.
definitions.meaning2: A line with sharp turns, like a Z. Example: She drew a zigzag on her paper.
definitions.studentChallenge: The little bug will ___ across the sand.

definitions.meaning1: To get twisted up in knots. Example: Long string can tangle if you drop it.
definitions.meaning2: A messy knot. Example: There was a tangle of yarn in the basket.
definitions.studentChallenge: Please do not let the cords ___ behind the desk.

definitions.meaning1: To pull on something with a quick, small pull. Example: I tug on the rope to ring the bell.
definitions.meaning2: A quick pull. Example: She gave the rope a tug.
definitions.studentChallenge: I felt a little ___ on my sleeve.

definitions.meaning1: To wave up and down, like wings. Example: Birds flap their wings to fly.
definitions.meaning2: A loose piece that hangs down. Example: The flap of the tent was open.
definitions.studentChallenge: The duck will ___ its wings and fly away.

definitions.meaning1: A shape like a circle made by a line or string. Example: Make a loop with the ribbon.
definitions.meaning2: To make a circle shape. Example: I loop the string around the stick.
definitions.studentChallenge: Make a ___ with the ribbon, like a circle.

definitions.meaning1: With a lot of wind. Example: It is a windy day, so hold your hat.
definitions.studentChallenge: It was so ___ that my hat blew away.

definitions.meaning1: With a soft, gentle wind. Example: A breezy morning is nice for a walk.
definitions.studentChallenge: It was a cool, ___ day, and the leaves moved a little.

definitions.meaning1: To pull very hard and fast. Example: Dad had to yank the stuck door open.
definitions.meaning2: A hard, fast pull. Example: With one yank, the box came open.
definitions.studentChallenge: I had to ___ hard to get my boot off.

definitions.meaning1: The sound of something moving fast through the air. Example: We heard a whoosh as the bike zoomed by.
definitions.meaning2: To move fast with that sound. Example: The bike will whoosh past us.
definitions.studentChallenge: The train went by with a loud ___.

definitions.meaning1: To spin around and around fast. Example: Leaves whirl in the wind.
definitions.meaning2: A fast spin. Example: The dancer did a whirl.
definitions.studentChallenge: I like to ___ in a circle until I am dizzy.

definitions.meaning1: To wave your arms or legs about in a wild way. Example: He had to flail his arms to keep from falling.
definitions.studentChallenge: The baby will ___ her arms and legs when she is happy.
